name.text: Angle between a sloping edge and the base

questiontext.text:
{@ctx@} is a right pyramid VABCD on a rectangular base with AB = {@ll@} and BC = {@ww@} {@un@}. [[if test="isH"]]Its height VO is {@gv@} {@un@}.[[else]]Each sloping edge is {@gv@} {@un@} long.[[/if]] M is the midpoint of BC.

(a) The projection of VA on the base is

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the angle between VA and the base.

[[input:ans2]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

Give lengths correct to 2 decimal places and angles correct to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the final answer.

generalfeedback.text:
(a) V is vertically above O, so the perpendicular from V lands at O and the projection of VA on the base is OA.

(b) OA is half of the diagonal AC: \(\mathrm{OA}^2 = \frac{{@ll@}^2 + {@ww@}^2}{4} = {@SA@}\), OA = {@d2(OA)@} {@un@}. Triangle VOA has a right angle at O, so [[if test="isH"]]\(\tan \mathrm{VAO} = \frac{\mathrm{VO}}{\mathrm{OA}} = \frac{{@gv@}}{\sqrt{{@SA@}}}\)[[else]]\(\cos \mathrm{VAO} = \frac{\mathrm{OA}}{\mathrm{VA}} = \frac{\sqrt{{@SA@}}}{{@gv@}}\)[[/if]] and the angle between VA and the base is \({@d1(th)@}^\circ\).

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: angle between a sloping edge and the base

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Name the projection of a sloping edge of a rectangular-based right pyramid on the base, then find the angle between the edge and the base.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 34, Section B, question B12(b)(ii) of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: rectangular bases given by height or sloping edge, new contexts and numbers, a naming step, randomised, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: kAC: is(ans1 = "AC"); kOM: is(ans1 = "OM"); kVO: is(ans1 = "VO");

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="kAC"]]

AC is the whole diagonal of the base. The projection of VA starts at A and ends at the foot of the perpendicular from V to the base. Is V vertically above C?

[[else]][[if test="kOM"]]

OM runs to the middle of a side: it is the projection of VM, not of VA.

[[else]][[if test="kVO"]]

VO is the perpendicular from V to the base.

[[else]]

AB lies in the base but V is not above B.

[[/if]][[/if]][[/if]]

feedbackvariables.text: okr: is(ans2 > 0 and ans2 < 90); rdn: float(ans2*%pi/180); oav: if okr then (if isH then float(gv/tan(rdn)) else float(gv*cos(rdn))) else NA;

truefeedback.text: That is the slope of the face VBC, using OM, the distance to the middle of a side. VA goes to the corner A, so use the distance from O to that corner.
That is the slope of the face VAB, using ON, the distance to the middle of a side. VA goes to the corner A, so use the distance from O to that corner.
You used the whole diagonal AC. O is its midpoint.
That is angle AVO, between VA and the vertical.
Your calculator is set to radians. Set it to degrees (DEG) and work out the angle again.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end, then round the angle once.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

Triangle VOA has a right angle at O. With your angle at A and [[if test="isH"]]VO[[else]]VA[[/if]] = {@gv@} {@un@}, OA would be {@d2(oav)@} {@un@}. OA runs from the centre O of the base to the corner A: compare your value with half the diagonal of the {@ll@} by {@ww@} base.

[[else]]

An angle between two lines, or between a line or plane and a plane, is between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]
